results.corrected_title: Replit makes OpenAI the default model for Replit Agent; CEO says it no longer works with Anthropic
results.corrected_summary: Speaking on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday 15 October 2026, Replit CEO Amjad Masad said Replit is no longer working with Anthropic. He said the decision was 'based on both cost, partnership, and performance' and argued that OpenAI's models now do better on Replit's own benchmark. He later told TechCrunch that Replit 'remains model agnostic' and that customers can still pick Anthropic models, but OpenAI is now the preferred partner and the default for Replit Agent. Sources familiar with the partnership disputed his account and said it is still in place.
key_facts: Remarks made on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday 15 Oct 2026; TechCrunch published on 16 Oct and updated on 17 Oct
Masad's stated reasons: cost, partnership and performance; 'I think ChatGPT is better now'
Clarification: customers can still use Claude models, but OpenAI is now the default and preferred partner for Replit Agent
Masad said Replit had recently been one of Anthropic's top five customers; Replit announced its OpenAI partnership in August
Enterprise share of revenue rose from about 2% last year to about 15% this year; more than 50% of revenue is B2B; no ARR figures disclosed
Insiders disputed his account; a late-September Replit blog post still listed Claude models running in production
results.issues: The candidate date of 2026-10-16 is when the article was published. The remarks themselves were made on Thursday 15 October. The 'no longer working with Anthropic' framing is contested: Masad himself walked it back to 'OpenAI is the default', and insiders say the Anthropic partnership is still in place. Only one outlet (TechCrunch) confirms this.

results.corrected_title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-Live-1.1 to ChatGPT Voice with 13 new voices
results.corrected_summary: On 15 October 2026 OpenAI began a gradual rollout of GPT-Live-1.1, an update to its GPT-Live voice model, in ChatGPT Voice. The update adds 13 new voices: two each in French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean and Mexican Spanish, plus one new English voice. It also makes accents sound more natural. Paid plans get the full GPT-Live-1.1 model, while Free (and reportedly Go) users get a lighter version called GPT-Live-1.1 Quip. GPT-Live-1.1 is not yet in the API; OpenAI says it is coming soon.
key_facts: Gradual rollout began on 15 Oct 2026 on web, iOS and Android; secondary reports say it also covers Codex and dots
13 new voices: two each in French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean and Mexican Spanish, plus the English voice 'Bubbie'
Plus, Pro and Business get GPT-Live-1.1; Free and Go get the smaller GPT-Live-1.1 Quip
Plus limit reported as 3 hours of GPT-Live-1.1 per rolling 24 hours
Not yet in the API: OpenAI says 1.1 is 'coming soon'; the earlier GPT-Live-1 has been in the API since 10 Sep
results.issues: I could not open OpenAI's own announcement or release notes, and Notebookcheck returned 403. The facts are confirmed through DataNorth and several consistent secondary outlets. The 13 new voices span seven languages: six non-English plus one English voice. Sources disagree slightly on plan limits (one lists 3 hours for Go as well as Plus, and 15 hours for Pro). One outlier source claims API availability; treat that as unconfirmed.

results.corrected_title: Cursor cloud agents can now build shareable interactive canvases
results.corrected_summary: A Cursor changelog entry dated 16 October 2026 says cloud agents can now build interactive canvases as part of their work, and a finished canvas can be shared with a team via a link. Cursor also launched an Environments API in beta for creating and managing cloud agent environments programmatically. Environments now support up to 300 repositories, and large environments load 5x faster.
key_facts: Cloud agents can build interactive canvases that can be shared by link
Environments API launched in beta for programmatic management of cloud environments
Cloud agent environments support up to 300 repositories
results.issues: Confirmed only from Cursor's own changelog. The changelog does not specifically mention 'dashboards/reports' as canvas examples, so that detail is left out.
